Repair request policy with peer selection, deduplication, and latency bucket management.

# Purpose
This C file implements the repair policy logic for a forest data structure. It creates and manages a `fd_policy_t` object in shared memory, then uses it to choose repair requests for missing data. The main entry point, [`fd_policy_next`](<#fd_policy_next>), scans the forest, applies deduplication with a time-based timeout, and builds repair messages for orphan slots, highest-shred requests, or specific shred requests. It also applies a throttle rule in [`passes_throttle_threshold`](<#passes_throttle_threshold>) so repair requests wait until a slot has aged enough before the code sends a request. The file uses a nonce counter and peer selection logic to spread requests across peers.

The file also manages peer state for repair traffic. It supports peer insert, query, remove, request update, and response update operations through [`fd_policy_peer_insert`](<#fd_policy_peer_insert>), [`fd_policy_peer_query`](<#fd_policy_peer_query>), [`fd_policy_peer_remove`](<#fd_policy_peer_remove>), [`fd_policy_peer_request_update`](<#fd_policy_peer_request_update>), and [`fd_policy_peer_response_update`](<#fd_policy_peer_response_update>). Peer records track request and response counts, timestamps, latency totals, and bucket placement in fast or slow lists. The code keeps peer selection state in [`fd_policy_peer_select`](<#fd_policy_peer_select>), which rotates through latency buckets when it chooses the next peer for a repair message.
